subject: SLO sampling harness, measurement methodology, and service credit scenarios
messages:

Subject: RFP follow-up: SLA measurement & credit calc examples

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the RFP response packet. Before we move to commercial terms the security and procurement teams have two technical asks that will be gating for us: 1) a concise description of how Redwood measures uptime and latency for multi-tenant hosted customers (primary telemetry source, sampling, and reconciliation with customer telemetry), and 2) worked examples that show how minutes of downtime map to monthly service credits under your proposed SLA bands.

Can you send a short methodology plus an example credit table (we need to present to legal by next Thursday)? Also, please indicate whether measurement windows are rolling 30d or calendar-month.

Best,
Anna

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Anna Patel <anna.patel@acmecorp.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: SLA measurement & credit calc examples

Anna —

Thanks for the clear asks. Summarized below is the methodology we use in hosted Redwood API (we will attach a worked spreadsheet and a short telemetry diagram). If this matches what your team needs I can ask Marcus (Reliability) to join the call and walk through edge cases.

High level (short):
- Primary metric source: Redwood platform telemetry (ingested at edge proxies and gateway layer) with immutable event ids and timestamps.
- Sampling: no sampling for availability checks — all 5xx / connection failures are counted. For latency SLOs we maintain full per-request histograms for production routes; for long-tail analysis we compute exact percentiles via T-Digest on aggregated events (not sampled).
- Reconciliation: we support an optional secure log export (S3) and a joint reconciliation job where customer telemetry can be compared to Redwood's event stream. Discrepancies are reconciled with mutually agreed rule sets; last-resort arbitration uses immutable logs and request ids.
- Measurement window: default is rolling 30-day window unless the contract specifies calendar-month. Rolling window is what we recommend for more stable SLO evaluation.
- Downtime definition: a minute is 'unavailable' if >90% of requests to a route return 5xx or if gateway rejects >50% of new connections to that route for that minute.

Attachments: SLA_Calculation_Sheet.xlsx (worked examples), telemetry-sampling-diagram.pdf (telemetry flow).

Let me know if you want Marcus on a quick call Friday.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Director, GTM Engineering

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: SLA measurement & credit calc examples

Anna —

Following up with the concrete measurement & credit math you asked for. Below is the concise methodology and a worked example taken from the attached spreadsheet (SLA_Calculation_Sheet.xlsx). If you want, we can export the raw hour-by-hour counts for your audit team.

Measurement methodology (concise):
1) Anchors: availability events are recorded at the edge gateway (reverse proxy) and include request_id, route_id, status_code, duration_ms, and the iso_minute bucket. Runtime-level errors (OOM, worker crash) generate an additional runtime_error event; both are considered in availability math.
2) Aggregation: events are bucketed into 1-minute iso buckets. For each minute and each customer route we compute success_rate = successful_requests / total_requests. A minute is marked unavailable if success_rate < 0.10 (i.e., >=90% failures) OR if total_requests drops by >70% vs 95th percentile baseline for that route (protects against routing blackholes).
3) Latency SLOs: per-route latency percentiles computed over rolling 30d using T-Digest snapshots. Example SLO: P95 < 250ms for 'standard' generation route.
4) Credits: monthly credit is proportional to minutes unavailable during the measurement window (rolling 30d by default). Example banding in sheet:
   - 99.99% availability or above: 0% credit
   - 99.9% - 99.99%: 5% of monthly fee
   - 99.0% - 99.9%: 10% of monthly fee
   - <99.0%: 25% of monthly fee

Worked example (calendar-month = 30 days for calc):
- Total minutes in window: 30 * 24 * 60 = 43,200
- If unavailable minutes observed = 43 -> availability = (43200 - 43)/43200 = 99.9% => credit = 5%
- If unavailable minutes observed = 432 -> availability = 99.0% => credit = 10%
- If unavailable minutes observed = 2,160 -> availability = 95.0% => credit = 25%

Notes on reconciliation and dispute:
- We provide the raw minute-bucket CSV and event log for the disputed window.
- If customer provides matching request_ids showing different outcomes, we run the joint reconciliation job and provide a reconciliation report.

I[0m
Marcus Lin
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

A couple of follow-ups before we present: 1) in your availability minute test you use a 90% failure threshold for marking a minute as unavailable — can you point us to the rationale & whether that threshold is configurable? 2) For latency SLOs, do you calculate percentiles using only successful requests or include error responses in the latency distribution?

Also, we have an internal audit requirement to see an example reconciliation: show us a sample minute where our telemetry reports success but Redwood shows 5xx — what fields are in the export we would receive?

Would prefer a short call next Thursday afternoon to finalize.

—Anna

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, priyom_das@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-22T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: SLA measurement & credit calc examples

Anna —

Answers inline and we attached a short "reconciliation manifest" example in the spreadsheet and the telemetry diagram for clarity.

1) 90% failure threshold rationale: we picked 90% to avoid noisy single-request blips influencing minute-level availability. It is configurable per contract; common alternatives clients pick are 50% (strict) or 75% (balanced). We can add a contract clause that allows Acme to specify the threshold and we will honor that for your account.

2) Percentiles: latency percentiles for SLOs are computed over successful responses only; errors are treated separately and count toward availability. For P95 latency we exclude 4xx/5xx. We document both distributions in our export (successful_latency_ms and error_count per minute).

3) Reconciliation export fields (what you'll receive): iso_minute, request_id, route_id, client_ip_hash, status_code, duration_ms, proxy_node_id, event_received_ts, checksum, raw_payload_ref (if enabled). See the attached spreadsheet sample for a mocked minute where the customer's telemetry shows 100% success but Redwood logged 5xx (we include request_ids for both sides).

Next steps: I attached Acme-MAP-20270422.xlsx (mutual action plan) with a proposed timeline and a DocuSign link for standard hosted terms with rolling-30d measurement. If that looks good let's confirm Thurs 4/29 2pm PT for a finalize call — Marcus will walk the audit team through the reconciliation manifest.

Thanks,
Soojin
